gaps.target_position: Falsification-test TAC input ($23-29B, central $26B): the scaling method holds 'Apple's share of Alphabet's distribution-partner TAC constant' from the 2022 court-found $20B figure forward via Alphabet's aggregate TAC CAGR (6.6%). The TAC investigator names this constant-share assumption as explicitly unverifiable and as the #1 thing that would change the position.
search_queries: Alphabet 10-K distribution partner TAC disaggregated Apple Samsung Mozilla breakdown 2024 2025
Apple Google search default deal revenue share renegotiated 2023 2024 2025
Google traffic acquisition costs distribution partners concentration Apple percentage decline
gaps.rationale: If Apple's share of Alphabet's distribution-partner TAC has fallen since 2022 (e.g., because Samsung, Mozilla or other partners renegotiated better terms, or because Alphabet's own disclosures show partner TAC growing slower than total TAC), the $26B central estimate is overstated and the falsification test's headline 19.7-28.3% of gross profit shrinks -- directly undermining the central quantitative claim the whole draft rests on. This is the single most load-bearing unverified assumption in the sizing chain; Alphabet's 10-K MD&A occasionally comments on partner concentration and should be checked directly rather than assumed unchanged.

gaps.target_position: Tension 1 / cross-locus convergence: 'AI query migration is already underway inside the 2-5 year window' rests entirely on ONE data point -- Eddy Cue's testimony that Safari search-query volume declined for the first time in 22 years, GenAI-attributed. Both the TAC and Lock-in investigators independently flag a second/third consecutive year of decline (or a reversal) as the thing that would most change their position.
search_queries: Safari search query volume 2026 trend decline continued OR reversed
Apple Safari search share StatCounter 2026 second half
Google search query volume growth 2026 AI chatbot cannibalization data
gaps.rationale: This single data point is doing outsized argumentative work: it reframes the report's central question (courts vs. interface) and overturns contradiction-cluster 5's 'long-horizon tail' verdict. Finding evidence the decline was a one-off (e.g., iOS version release timing, a Safari bug, a one-time methodology change in how Google or Apple counts queries) or evidence of a rebound would materially weaken Tension 1's central reframing and the AI-migration risk weighting in the falsification test's caveats. Conversely, a second down year would let the draft assert the trend with much higher confidence instead of hedging on n=1.

gaps.target_position: Hardware locus commits: FY2026 iPhone strength is overwhelmingly ASP/mix, not units (IDC: shipments +4.9% vs. Apple iPhone revenue +23.3%, ~17.5pp attributed to ASP/mix) -- resting on ONE clean calendar-aligned quarter (CY Q4 2025 / Apple FQ1 2026). The investigator names an IDC/Counterpoint release with calendar-Q1/Q2-2026 Apple-specific units as the thing that would most weaken this reading.
search_queries: IDC Counterpoint Apple iPhone unit shipments calendar Q1 2026
IDC Counterpoint Apple iPhone unit shipments calendar Q2 2026
Apple iPhone 17 sell-through units growth 2026 Canalys
gaps.rationale: This is one of the four minimum components the query demands (services CAGR needed to hold growth flat as hardware matures) and it directly feeds Tension 3's 'cost pass-through, low-quality growth' framing plus the KeyBanc price-led-vs-volume-led multiple argument. If more recent calendar-quarter data shows units accelerating alongside revenue (not just the single Q4 2025 print), the 'price not volume' reading needs softening and the draft's claim that FY2026 growth is low-quality cost pass-through is overstated.

gaps.rationale: The draft commits hard to commission economics being permanently impaired, but no source in the corpus yet estimates what a 'cost-based' fee under the Ninth Circuit's own standard would actually be -- comparisons.md itself flags this as 'the single most decision-relevant future number [that] does not yet exist.'
